packages/rekordbox-live/src/setup-assist.content: This is billed as a realistic 60 Hz / 500 ms stream, but the only assertions are `received > 0` and the last address; the packet count and `updateHz` are never checked, so a regression in `sampleFromProvider` (e.g. reading `updateHz` as 0 because `status.state`/`updateHz` is misread) or silently dropped datagrams would still pass. It also depends on the sibling `.ts` sources existing at runtime — `readFileSync` throws if tests run from a build without them.

packages/serato/src/capture.test.ts.content: The busy-wait silently gives up when the deadline passes: the loop condition only stops looping, it never records that the wait timed out. On a slow/loaded machine the test then proceeds with a partial capture and fails later with an unrelated assertion (or a confusing `compareSequences` diff) instead of a clear timeout. The fixed 3000 ms budget is also arbitrary. Assert the invariant after the loop so a timeout is reported explicitly.

Burst grouping here is driven by wall-clock arrival times, not script time. `inbound` frames are stamped by the proxy with `atMs: Date.now()` (capture.ts), while `playAction("two-decks", 50)` compresses the script gaps (up to 80 ms between steps) to <=2 ms of wall time. `replaySeratoFrames(..., "1x")` regroups frames using a 50 ms gap on those wall-clock stamps (`seratoBursts`), so if CI stalls >=50 ms between two sends of the same track load, one load splits into two bursts, `replaySeratoFrames` emits two generations per deck, and the `captured.map(deckId)).toEqual(live.map(deckId))` assertion fails even though the decoder is correct. Note that `sendAt` deliberately stamps script time to prevent exactly this, but the capture path replaces it with wall time. Make the replay grouping deterministic (e.g. rebuild `atMs` from the emulator's script timeline, or replay the whole capture as a single burst) so the comparison exercises the decoder rather than CI jitter.

`withoutStamp` duplicates the helper already exported by `./replay.js` (identical signature and body). Import it from `./replay.js` (next to `replaySeratoFrames`/`splitFrames`) instead of re-declaring it so the two implementations cannot drift.

If one cleanup rejects (e.g. a socket already errored), the exception aborts the loop right after that entry was popped, so the remaining cleanups never run and their servers/sockets leak into the rest of the process, potentially interfering with other test files. Run every cleanup even when one fails.

packages/show-planner/src/events.test.ts.content: The fixture is force-cast with `as unknown as TrackModel`, so it is never validated against `trackModelSchema` (which is `.strict()` and enforces the `musicalEventTypeSchema` union, `beatGrid` shape, `identity` shape, etc.).
